evidence.title: Town of Morris, Connecticut -- Zoning Moratorium on Battery Energy Storage Systems and Data Centers
evidence.publisher: Town of Morris, Connecticut, Planning and Zoning Commission
evidence.supports: This is the operative moratorium text (identical to the earlier draft), confirming a 12-month duration running from the effective date of adoption, and that the effective date itself is defined as the date of newspaper publication and Town Clerk filing under Connecticut General Statutes. The document's presence in the Commission's 'regulations' folder (as distinct from the 'generals'/draft folder it occupied in mid-April) indicates the Commission moved this from draft to adopted status.
evidence.quote: Section 6. Duration. This Moratorium shall remain in effect for a period of twelve (12) months from the effective date of adoption, unless earlier terminated or extended in accordance with applicable law. ... Section 9. Effective Date. This Moratorium shall become effective upon publication in a newspaper of general circulation and filing with the Town Clerk in accordance with Connecticut General Statutes.

evidence.title: Morris, Connecticut Imposes Two-Year Data Center Moratorium to Protect Farmland
evidence.supports: Reports that the Morris Planning and Zoning Commission approved the moratorium following a public hearing held on a Tuesday, corroborating adoption in the May 2026 timeframe, though its characterization of the duration as 'two years' conflicts with the 12-month term stated in the operative text.
evidence.quote: The Planning and Zoning Commission in Morris just approved a two-year moratorium on data centers.

decisions.notes: Duration (365 days / 12 months) in the existing inventory row is confirmed correct directly from the adopted ordinance text, notwithstanding press coverage that mischaracterizes it as a 'two-year moratorium' -- I am not changing duration_days. What has changed is that adoption itself is now reasonably established (whereas the prior record treated adoption as fully unverified), even though the precise adoption date, the newspaper-publication/effective date, and hence the exact computed expiration remain unconfirmed. Based on a 12-month term running from an effective date somewhere around May 2026, expiration would fall approximately in May 2027, but this is an estimate, not a confirmed date, and computed_expiry is left to the merge pipeline rather than asserted here.
